killedBy: createLevelSystem: pp1Roles reaches the built world (issue #358, composition not unit) pp1Roles=1 reaches the player tank in a campaign world, on BOTH axes
createLevelSystem: pp1Roles reaches the built world (issue #358, composition not unit) reaches every tank of a real two-player coop world, co-players included
why:
Drops issue #358's role-matrix arm from the ONE call that carries it into a campaign world, which is the shape a trailing positional invites: `createWorldFor` takes it eighth in a long list, so a lost argument is silently `undefined` rather than a type error, and `?dev=1&pp1Roles=1` then plays the shipped roster while the menu says the arm is on -- a flag that changes a value and not the game. MEASURED while landing this: with the argument removed, all 89 cases across levels.test.ts, pp1-roles.test.ts and dev-config.test.ts stayed green, because those two prove only that loadArena stamps a cap and that the refusal reads one. Caught by the campaign case and its two-player coop sibling, named in killedBy; the flag-off control survives by design, since dropping the argument and leaving the flag off are the same world.

RE-ANCHORED at issue #493, which replaced this builder's positional argument list with one `WorldForInit` object. The old `find` quoted the positional run and reported FAILED-TO-APPLY on CI -- the silent form of an entry that has stopped measuring anything, and the reason this one was caught by `verify (current)` rather than by a local `--only` selection naming only the entries already known to be affected. WHAT MOVED AND WHAT DID NOT: the sentence above about a trailing positional being lost 'silently `undefined` rather than a type error' no longer describes the call -- there are no positionals left to lose. The property it rests on SURVIVES in the key form, which is why this is re-anchored rather than retired: an omitted or `undefined` key in `WorldForInit` is exactly as silent as a dropped positional was, since every key is optional by design. Spelled as `pp1Roles: undefined` rather than as a deletion so the mutation is the flag failing to arrive, not the object changing shape.
